The first public release of IntelX, the code for *IntelX: Autonomous Indoor Exploration via Local Coverage Gain Prediction and Structure-Aware Planning* (under review).

**In it**

- The 2D simulator with CUDA ray casting, the coverage-gain regressor (a U-Net with a ResNet-34 encoder) and the IntelX policy: the local planner, junction verification and the global planner.
- Every method the paper compares, in the same simulator and from the same spawns: Random Frontier, Nearest Frontier, Cost-Utility, Geometric IG, Frontier (AutoX), and MapEx, UPEN and IG-Hector through the MapEx service.
- The paired benchmark. `SUBMITTED_BEHAVIOUR` restores the behaviour the submitted results were produced with.
- Data collection, training and evaluation for the regressor.

**Downloads**

- The trained checkpoint, [`checkpoint_best.pth`](https://utdallas.box.com/s/2tuurbusuawkowwe9rjnmsbkhtgm6b5o) (293.4 MB, sha256 `4f82a3fa54a0349720b2b3c42ee812ea744d539060146fbd2be8ca16d6a69ed4`).
- The test, out-of-distribution and real maps, in the [Box folder](https://utdallas.box.com/s/stgu95mdcf3p7tgp5z5a53pcxiuwrplu).
- The 18 training maps and the coverage dataset (about 1 TB) are not public yet.

**Get started**

[Documentation](https://irvlutd.github.io/IntelX/docs/) · [Project page](https://irvlutd.github.io/IntelX/)

```bash
git clone --recursive https://github.com/IRVLUTD/IntelX.git
```

`--recursive` fetches MapEx, which the prediction baselines need. The source archives below leave that submodule out.
